content: A clinical site is a medical facility where clinical research is conducted under the supervision of a clinical investigator, who must be a licensed medical doctor (MD). To qualify as a clinical site, the facility must adhere to strict regulations established by the International Conference on Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) and other regulatory authorities. According to ICH GCP 4.1.1, the clinical investigator must possess the necessary qualifications, which include appropriate education, training, and experience, to take responsibility for the proper conduct of the clinical trial. The investigator must meet all regulatory requirements and provide evidence of their qualifications, such as an up-to-date curriculum vitae or other relevant documentation, as requested by the trial sponsor, the institutional review board (IRB) or independent ethics committee (IEC), and/or regulatory authorities. Per ICH GCP 4.1.2, the investigator must have a thorough understanding of the investigational product(s) being studied. This includes familiarity with the clinical protocol, the current Investigator's Brochure, product information, and any other materials provided by the sponsor. As stated in ICH GCP 4.1.3, the investigator is required to be fully aware of and comply with Good Clinical Practice guidelines and all applicable regulatory requirements. ICH GCP 4.1.4 mandates that the investigator and the clinical site must allow monitoring and auditing by the trial sponsor, as well as inspections by the relevant regulatory authorities. Finally, according to ICH GCP 4.1.5, the investigator is responsible for maintaining a list of individuals who are appropriately qualified to whom significant trial-related duties have been delegated.
